name: find_app_steps
title: Find steps in AppForShare
description: Where to click in the AppForShare dashboard or site for a task ("how do I add a tester", "where are API tokens"): exact page, button names and numbered steps, plus whether this account can do it on its plan and team role and how to unlock it. Read only. Use it before saying AppForShare cannot do something.

name: whoami
title: Who am I
description: The account, plan and role this AppForShare token works in, and whether the workspace requires two step sign in for members (read only; the rule is set in the dashboard).

name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: Projects (one per app and platform) in the account, newest first, with their ids.

name: list_builds
title: List builds
description: Recent builds with install link, version, size, installs, store readiness status, channels and the known malware check status.

platform.description: Only builds of this platform (macos and windows = desktop builds, Pro and Team)

app.description: Bundle id (iOS, macOS) or package name (Android, Windows MSIX)

channel.description: Channel name such as beta or live: builds in that channel, newest put in first

name: latest_build
title: Latest build
description: The newest build matching the filters, with its install link, release notes and store readiness findings.

platform.description: Only builds of this platform (macos and windows = desktop builds, Pro and Team)

app.description: Bundle id (iOS, macOS) or package name (Android, Windows MSIX)

channel.description: Channel name such as beta or live: builds in that channel, newest put in first

name: build_info
title: Build details and store readiness
description: One build: install link, version, installs, release notes, permissionsPlain (each permission in plain words: what it lets the app do, the app's own iOS reason verbatim, and isNew against the previous build of the app; facts, not a safety verdict) and the store readiness check (App Store and Google Play rules) with a fix for each finding. Expo apps also get their Expo facts (SDK, expo-updates runtime version, update channel and URL, development client) and the Expo checks (development build shared with testers, test build on the production channel, runtime version against native changes). Flutter apps also get their Flutter facts (build mode, engine and Dart version, obfuscation hint, Impeller flag) and the Flutter checks (debug or profile build shared with testers). malwareScan is the check for known malware run on every upload (status pending, clean, flagged, error or skipped, and scannedAt; it only finds malware that is already known, and a flagged build is held for staff review). desktop is set for macOS and Windows builds (Pro and Team): file kind, SHA-256, minimum OS, architectures, signature (developer-id, apple, adhoc, signed, unsigned) and signer, notarization ticket stapled or not (macOS), publisher and package name; testers download the file from the install page, and readiness lists unsigned, ad hoc signed and not notarized files. Guidance only, not a promise of store approval.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: get_security_scan
title: Security scan of a build
description: Security scan of one build, read at upload from the .ipa or .apk: hardcoded secrets (only the kind, the file and a masked value, never the full key), Android backup, exported components, R8 hint, WebView debugging and user certificates, iOS App Transport Security exceptions, symbols and get-task-allow, root, jailbreak and tamper libraries, and library versions with a known advisory. Each finding has a level (block, warn, info), an OWASP MASVS category, a detail and a fix; the summary counts them ("1 to fix, 3 warnings"). Findings and hints from a static scan, not a penetration test or a certification. Builds uploaded before the scan say status unknown. Read only. Pro and Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: get_install_badge
title: Download button for a README
description: A download button for a README or docs page: Markdown and HTML snippets with a 200 x 60 "Install test build" badge (dark and light) that links to the install page of a build, or to a channel link. For a channel the badge is live: it shows the version of the newest build in the channel (refreshed every 5 minutes) and the link always opens that build. Give a build id or install link slug, or a channel address (the part after /c/). The link carries ?ref=badge so visits from the button show in analytics. The badge says "test build" and never names a store. Read only. Free and up for builds; channels need Pro or Team.

target.description: Build id, install link slug, or channel address (the part after /c/)

name: build_installs
title: Who installed a build
description: Installs of one build, newest first (up to 200): device, OS version, model, country and the tester when known, with totals by device and country. Read only.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: build_install_issues
title: Why a tester cannot install a build
description: Why testers' phones may refuse one build: signing (App Store or unsigned), profile expired or ending soon, no devices in the profile, Developer Mode, enterprise trust, test key, plus the minimum iOS or Android version, and how many devices the profile lists. Use it to answer "my tester cannot install". Pass the tester's UDID to check their device too. Read only.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: export_test_plan
title: Export the test plan for Firebase or Maestro
description: The build's AI test plan as a file other tools run: format "firebase" gives Firebase App Testing agent test cases (YAML for firebase apptesting:execute --test-dir, Android only, preview), "maestro" a Maestro starter flow with a screenshot and an assertWithAI check per task. Needs a plan (test_plan with generate: true). Read only. Pro and Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: test_plan
title: Test plan for a build
description: The AI test plan of a build: up to 15 tasks ordered by risk, each with steps and the fact it comes from (a new permission, a minimum OS change, a readiness finding, the release notes), and which tasks the team ticked as done. Pass generate: true to write a new plan when there is none or the build changed; that uses 1 AI action of the account (Developer role). focus narrows it, for example "payments".

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

focus.description: Optional area to focus on, with generate

name: github_build_run
title: GitHub build runs and why one failed
description: iOS and Android builds AppForShare started on the workspace's GitHub Actions. Without run: the recent runs, newest first, with their result. With run (an id from that list): that run, and for a failed one the AI explanation of the likely cause and the fix steps, written from the failed job's log with secrets taken out (shown when AppForShare already made one). Pass explain: true to make one when there is none (1 AI action of the account, Developer role); it never changes code or the repository. Pro and Team.

explain.description: Make the AI explanation of a failed run when there is none (1 AI action)

name: list_feedback
title: Tester feedback
description: Feedback testers sent from install pages and the in-app link, and on Team the TestFlight screenshot and crash feedback read from App Store Connect: bug reports, suggestions and other notes, newest first, with the source (page, app or testflight), the device, OS, build (and the TestFlight build) and how many screenshots or recordings came with it (open them in the dashboard link), and on Team the reply thread (team replies and tester answers). Read only.

build.description: Optional build id or install link slug

blockers.description: Only reports marked as release blockers

source.description: Only reports from the install page, the in-app link, or TestFlight (Team)

name: recent_activity
title: Workspace activity
description: What happened in the workspace, newest first: uploads, channel changes, tester feedback, tasks, release checklist ticks, link controls and issues sent to trackers, each with who did it. Optional project id and kind. Read only. Team.

name: task_from_feedback
title: Make a task from tester feedback
description: Add a task to the project's task board from one feedback report, linked to its build. Once per report. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

name: send_feedback_to_tracker
title: Send tester feedback to Linear or Jira
description: Create an issue in the workspace's connected Linear or Jira from one feedback report, with its text, device facts and screenshots. A report is sent once; the answer has the issue key and link. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

name: resolve_feedback
title: Mark tester feedback resolved
description: Mark a feedback report as resolved (for example after the fix is in a new build), or open it again with reopen: true. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Developer role.

name: reply_to_feedback
title: Reply to tester feedback
description: Reply to one feedback report. The reply is kept in the report's thread and the tester gets one email in the language of their install page, with the reply and a link to answer once on the install page. Only for reports where the tester left an email address (not TestFlight reports); up to 20 messages per report and 5 replies per report a day. Write the reply the person asked for, plain text up to 2000 characters, and show it to them first; then pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

text.description: The reply, as the person approved it

name: release_checklist
title: Release checklist of a build
description: The workspace release checklist with what is ticked on this build, its named approvals (who approves each approval step, approved, rejected with a note, or pending), the open release blockers of its project, and whether the gated channel (Live by default) would take it. Read only: approvals are given only by the approver signed in to the dashboard, never by an AI tool. Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: release_overview
title: Release page of a version
description: One version of an app in one answer, like the release page: its iOS and Android builds with channels and store readiness, the release checklist and approvals of the newest build per platform, open release blockers from tester feedback, App Store and TestFlight state, Google Play tracks with rollout percentage, Android vitals (crash rate and ANR rate per version code from Google Play, Team, read only and never acted on), and a timeline of who did what. Give the version (like 2.4.0) and the app as its bundle id or package name, or a project id. Without a version it lists the versions. Read only. Team (Pro gets it without the checklist).

version.description: Version as in the build, like 2.4.0. Leave out to list versions.

app.description: Bundle id (iOS, macOS) or package name (Android, Windows MSIX)

name: tick_release_step
title: Tick a release checklist step
description: Tick (or untick with done: false) one step of the release checklist on a build, by its key from release_checklist. Only tick what the person says was really done. Approval steps (those with an approver) cannot be ticked or approved here; the approver answers them in the dashboard. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: promote_build
title: Put a build into a channel
description: Make a build the newest in a channel (for example beta or live) so the channel link and QR code open it. Using an older build rolls the link back; apps already installed are not changed. On Team the gated channel (Live by default) refuses a build until its release checklist is ticked and no release blocker is open; see release_checklist. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

channel.description: Channel name, created on first use

name: set_link_controls
title: Pause or limit an install link
description: Change the controls of one build's install link: pause or resume it, set a start time before which it takes no installs (testers see when it opens and can ask for one email then; ISO date time, null opens it now), a stop date after which it takes no installs (ISO date time, null removes it), or an install limit (null removes it). The start must be before the stop date. Leave out what should stay as it is. Builds already installed are not affected. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

paused.description: true pauses the link, false turns it back on

startAt.description: Opens for installs at this ISO 8601 date time, for example 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z, or null to open now

stopAt.description: ISO 8601 date time, for example 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z, or null for no stop date

maxInstalls.description: Install limit, or null for none

name: retire_build
title: Retire a test build
description: Mark one build as retired ("use a newer build"), for example when it crashes on start: its install link takes no installs, its page sends testers to the newest build of the same app and platform, channels skip it (a channel falls back to the build before), and the update check answers retired: true and minBuild for it. Optional reason (up to 200 characters) is shown to testers. undo: true brings it back. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

reason.description: Shown to testers, for example Crashes on login, use 2.5 (122)

undo.description: true brings a retired build back

name: list_build_links
title: List extra share links of a build
description: The extra share links of one build: label, URL, install count, whether a password is set, stop date, install cap and state (LIVE, or why it takes no installs), with the plan limit (Pro 3, Team 20 per build). Read only.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: add_build_link
title: Add an extra share link to a build
description: Make another install link for one build, for example one per client, with its own label, optional password (4 to 128 characters), optional start time and stop date (ISO date times, start before stop) and optional install cap. It opens the same install page with its own count; the build's pause, stop date and cap still apply. Returns the new URL. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro (3 per build) and Team (20 per build), Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

label.description: Name for the owner, for example Client A (testers do not see it)

expiresAt.description: Stop date, ISO 8601 date time, for example 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z

startAt.description: Opens for installs at this ISO 8601 date time, for example 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z

name: remove_build_link
title: Remove an extra share link
description: Turn off one extra share link (by its slug from list_build_links). Its page says the link was turned off; the build and its other links keep working. This cannot be undone. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Developer role.

name: list_access_codes
title: List access codes of a build or extra link
description: The per tester access codes of a build's own page (build id or slug) or of one extra link (its slug): label, devices used of the allowed count, state (ACTIVE, USED or REVOKED) and when it was made. The codes themselves are never shown again after they are made. Up to 25 per page. Team. Read only.

target.description: Build id, build slug, or the slug of an extra link

name: create_access_code
title: Create a per tester access code
description: Make a one off access code for a build's own page or for one extra link, with a label (the client or person it is for) and a device count (1 to 50, default 1). A tester types it on the install page instead of the shared password; each install takes one device off the code. Returns the code once: give it to the person, it cannot be shown again. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Owner or Admin role.

target.description: Build id, build slug, or the slug of an extra link

label.description: Who it is for, for example Ana at Client A (testers do not see it)

maxInstalls.description: Devices the code may install on (default 1)

name: revoke_access_code
title: Revoke an access code
description: Turn off one access code (by its id from list_access_codes). It stops opening the page at once; installs already made stay, and the shared password and other codes keep working. This cannot be undone. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Owner or Admin role.

name: set_channel_address
title: Pick a channel address
description: Give a channel its own address, for example /c/acme-beta: 3 to 40 lower case letters, digits and hyphens, unique on AppForShare. The old address keeps redirecting for 30 days and the in-app update check on it keeps working; old addresses are never given to anyone else. Name the app by bundle id (app) or project id. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

app.description: Bundle id or package name of the app

name: set_testflight_link
title: TestFlight link on a channel
description: Add the TestFlight public link (https://testflight.apple.com/join/...) to a channel such as beta, so iPhone and iPad visitors of the channel link go to TestFlight while Android visitors still get the newest APK, with one link and QR code. Pass url: null to remove it. Name the app by bundle id (app) or project id. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

channel.description: Channel name such as beta, created on first use

url.description: TestFlight public link, or null to remove it

app.description: Bundle id or package name of the app

name: channel_followers
title: Channel followers
description: How many people follow a channel by email ("Email me new builds" on its page): confirmed and pending counts, the plan cap and masked addresses (jo***@example.com), newest first. Followers confirm by email first and get one email per new build, at most one every 6 hours. Read only: removing a follower is in the dashboard or the CLI. Name the app by bundle id (app) or project id. Pro and Team.

app.description: Bundle id or package name of the app

name: delete_build
title: Delete a build
description: Delete a build. Its install link stops working at once; it can be restored from the dashboard for 7 days. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: restore_build
title: Restore a deleted build
description: Bring back a build that was deleted in the last 7 days: its install link works again with the same address. Without a build, lists the builds that can still be restored. Builds removed by AppForShare staff cannot be restored here. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Developer role.

build.description: Build id or slug of the deleted build; leave out to list what can be restored

name: resign_build
title: Re-sign an iOS build with a new profile
description: Re-sign an iOS build with a new provisioning profile, for example after new test iPhones were added to the ad hoc profile, so testers can install without a new build from Xcode or CI. AppForShare signs a copy with the workspace's signing certificate (an Admin adds the .p12 once in Settings) and saves it as a NEW build ("re-signed from build X", same release notes, new SHA-256); the original build and its sign-offs stay as they were. Bundle ID, version and build number never change. Profiles come from the connected App Store Connect key: pass profile names or ids, or leave out for the best active ad hoc, development or enterprise profile of the app. App Store profiles are refused. Without confirm: the check only (profiles, certificate, devices added or dropped, problems). With confirm: true (ask the person first) the re-sign is queued; follow it with build_info (resign.lastResign). Developer role. Pro and Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

profiles.description: Names or ids of profiles on the connected Apple account (optional; leave out for the best one for the app)

mergeEntitlements.description: Keep the app's own entitlements where the profile allows them (default: entitlements from the profile)

name: cleanup_preview
title: Preview a clean up of old builds
description: Which builds of a project an automatic clean up would move to the 7 day restore list right now, the storage it would free, and which old builds it keeps on purpose (newest build of each platform, a channel's current build, builds in a client delivery, builds sent to TestFlight or Google Play in the last 90 days, builds marked keep). Uses the project's saved rule, or keep (newest N per platform, 5 to 200) and olderDays (30, 60, 90 or 180) if given; with both, a build goes only when it breaks both. Read only: nothing is deleted. The rule is set on the project's Testing page; a person runs a clean up with the CLI (appforshare cleanup). Pro and Team.

keep.description: Keep the newest N builds per platform

olderDays.description: Remove builds older than this many days

name: list_webhooks
title: List webhooks and recent deliveries
description: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Discord, Telegram, Webex and generic webhooks of the workspace: name, kind, events, project, on or off, failures, last error, and with webhook (an id) its last 30 deliveries (event, delivered or failed, HTTP status, error). Never returns a webhook URL or signing secret. Adding or changing webhooks is done in the dashboard; a person can resend a delivery with the CLI (appforshare webhooks redeliver). Read only. Pro and Team, Owner or Admin.

webhook.description: Webhook id: also return its recent deliveries

name: create_upload_link
title: Make a one time upload link
description: Make a link where the person drops an .ipa, .apk or .aab (on Pro and Team also a desktop build: .dmg, .pkg, zipped .app, .msix, .msixbundle, .appx, .appxbundle or .msi) in a browser, for chat assistants that cannot read files on their computer. The link works once, for 30 minutes, on any device, without signing in; the build goes into this workspace as the person who connected, with the plan's limits. Give the person the url, then call check_upload with the ticket for the install link and store readiness. Optional release notes and a channel. Pro and Team, Developer role.

channel.description: Put the build into this channel (such as beta) when it is ready

name: upload_from_url
title: Upload a build from a URL
description: Upload an .ipa, .apk or .aab (or a desktop build: .dmg, .pkg, zipped .app, .msix, .msixbundle, .appx, .appxbundle, .msi) that is at a public https URL, such as a GitHub release asset or a signed CI artifact link: AppForShare checks the size first, then downloads it into this workspace. Links that need a sign in, plain http, and private or local addresses are refused. Returns a ticket; call check_upload with it for progress, the install link and store readiness. Optional release notes and a channel. Pro and Team, Developer role.

url.description: https URL of the build file (.ipa, .apk, .aab or a desktop build)

channel.description: Put the build into this channel (such as beta) when it is ready

name: check_upload
title: Result of an upload link or URL upload
description: State of an upload started with create_upload_link or upload_from_url in this workspace: waiting (link not used yet), expired, uploading (with bytes received), processing, ready (install link, and the store readiness check with a fix for each finding) or failed (with the reason). Read only.

name: email_build_link
title: Email the install link
description: Email one build's install link to up to 5 addresses (one plain mail each, no tracking; an address that already got this build is skipped). Not for private projects: add testers there. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Developer role. Pro and Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: release_status
title: App Store and Google Play release status
description: Release status of the apps shared from connected App Store Connect and Google Play accounts: App Store versions and review state, recent TestFlight builds, Google Play tracks and rollout, plus recent changes. Read only. Pro and Team.

app.description: Optional bundle id, package name or app name to narrow the result

name: list_reviews
title: Store reviews
description: Customer reviews of the shared App Store and Google Play apps from the reviews inbox. Read only: replies are written and posted by a person in the dashboard. Pro and Team.

name: list_testers
title: List testers
description: Testers of the workspace with their projects and groups, optionally only those of one project (id) or one group (name). Read only. Team.

name: list_tester_groups
title: List tester groups
description: Tester groups of the workspace with member counts and the projects each group can install. Read only. Team.

name: add_testers
title: Add testers
description: Add email addresses as testers, optionally to a project (id) and to tester groups (names). New testers get an invite email unless notify is false. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

name: remove_testers
title: Remove testers
description: With a project id: take away the access given by hand to that project (access through a group stays). Without: remove the testers from the workspace. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

name: share_build_with_testers
title: Share a build with groups and testers
description: Give tester groups (names) and testers (emails) the project of an uploaded build and email them its install link. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Team, Developer role.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: release_defaults
title: Saved release defaults of store apps
description: Saved release defaults of the shared App Store and Google Play apps: What's New per language, phased release on or off (App Store), and the Google Play track and rollout percent used when promoting. They only fill in forms; nothing is sent to a store from them. Without app, every shared app. Read only. Pro and Team.

app.description: Bundle id, package name or app id from release_status (optional)

store.description: Only when the same bundle id is on both stores

name: set_release_defaults
title: Save release defaults of a store app
description: Save the release defaults of one shared store app: whatsNew (list of { language, text }, replaces the saved list; App Store up to 4000 characters, Google Play 500), phased (App Store, true or false), playTrack and playPercent (Google Play; percent 100 = everyone, null = draft). Fields left out keep their value; null clears one. Only saved in AppForShare, never sent to a store. Ask the person first and pass confirm: true. Pro and Team, Developer role.

app.description: Bundle id, package name or app id

name: get_store_pages
title: Store pages of store apps
description: Store pages of the shared App Store and Google Play apps: the privacy policy, support and account deletion page addresses, status (draft, live, lapsing = the plan no longer covers it and it goes down on downAt, down), unpublished changes, what is still missing before publishing, and the facts read from the newest build (permissions in plain words, iOS reasons, recognised SDKs). The pages are written from the owner's answers; they are not legal advice and do not make an app compliant or approved by a store. Editing, the AI draft and publishing happen in the dashboard or the CLI, never from here. Without app, every shared app. Read only. Pro (one app) and Team (every app).

app.description: Bundle id, package name, app id or page address code (optional)

store.description: Only when the same bundle id is on both stores

name: rollout_plan
title: Scheduled Google Play rollout plans
description: Scheduled staged rollout plans of one shared Google Play app: release, steps (percent and hours after the step before), which steps are done, next step time, status (ACTIVE, PAUSED, HALTED by a safeguard, STOPPED, DONE) and why. Plans are set, paused, resumed and stopped by a person in the dashboard or the CLI, never from here. Read only. Team.

app.description: Package name or app id from release_status

name: store_upload_status
title: Store sends of a build (TestFlight, Google Play)
description: Whether a build can be sent to TestFlight (App Store signed .ipa) or a Google Play track (the kept .aab) and why not, the shared store app it would go to, and every send so far with its status (queued, sending, processing at Apple, finishing = waiting for Apple to process the build before the send options, sent, draft on Play production, failed) and the store answer. Each send lists the options the Admin picked (TestFlight What to Test, TestFlight groups and beta review on Team; Google Play release name, in-app update priority, changes not sent for review) and what happened to each. Sending and picking options is done by an Admin in the dashboard or with the CLI (appforshare store-upload, upload --store-upload), never from here. Read only. Pro and Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: intune_status
title: Microsoft Intune sends of a build
description: Whether a build can be sent to the workspace's Microsoft Intune as a line of business app (an enterprise or ad hoc signed .ipa, or an APK; App Store or development signed .ipa files and .aab uploads cannot) and why not, the status of the Intune connection (OK, ERROR with the reason in plain words, or not connected; never the client secret), and every send so far: new app or new version, Intune app name and id, status (queued, sending, sent, failed) and the result. AppForShare only hands the file to Intune; assignment to groups stays in Intune. Sending is done by an Admin in the dashboard or with the CLI (appforshare store-upload <build> --to intune --yes), never from here. Read only. Team.

build.description: Build id or the slug of its install link

name: android_store_status
title: Android store listing status
description: The AppForShare Android store listings of this workspace: status (DRAFT = setup not finished, READY = waiting for the first store build, LISTED, SUSPENDED) and what is still missing, the package name claim (verified, pending, failed with the reason, or disputed; a dispute is settled automatically from the evidence, proof of the signing key beating a repository token file), the source repository, tag and build variant, the releases with their status (QUEUED = waiting for the author's GitHub Actions build, PENDING = waiting for our own builder for GitLab and plain git sources, PENDING_REVIEW = APK received, automatic review checks running, IN_REVIEW = a clean update on its short hold before it is approved by itself, APPROVED = reviewed and ready for signing, SIGNING, SIGNED = signed APK stored with its SHA-256, size and certificate, PUBLISHED = live in the AppForShare store, SIGN_FAILED with the reason (retried by itself, then Try signing again in the Store tab), REJECTED with the reason and the fix; every release is reviewed automatically by our checks and an AI review, and staff can review any decision later; each release carries its review: decidedBy AUTO or STAFF, the reasons it needed a decision, the findings in plain words, the time of the automatic approval, the rejection reason, the fix, and whether the author can ask once for a re-review or use Recheck in the Store tab), the signing of the listing (mode STORE_KEY = AppForShare signs with a key made for this app, AUTHOR_SIGNS = the author signs each release with the CLI appforshare store sign, OWN_KEY = AppForShare signs with the imported keystore of the author, Team; the certificate SHA-256 users will see, fixed by the first signed release; never key material), the targets of each release (afs = the AppForShare store, play = Google Play, appstore = the App Store, each with its own status: WAITING, QUEUED, SENDING, PROCESSING, LIVE, DRAFT = a Play production draft, FAILED with the reason, WITHDRAWN; sends to Google Play and the App Store are made by an Admin in the Store tab or with the CLI appforshare store send, never from here), the GitHub Actions store builds (PENDING_REVIEW = accepted, REJECTED with the reason in plain words, SHA-256, versionCode, run link) with the workflow block to add to the repository, and the public page address. Without project or app, every store app in short. Setting up, claiming and starting releases happen in the Store tab of the project, never from here. No secrets (the webhook secret is never shown). Read only. Every plan with an account.

To publish, ask the person first and pass confirm: true. A first listing needs summary (up to 80 characters), categories, privacyPolicyUrl and ratingAnswers (all none for an app without mature content, ask the person); an update needs nothing but an optional changelog. A failed check answers check, message and fix. Every plan with an account; Developer role.

name: android_store_safety
title: Android store safety status
description: Trust and safety facts of one AppForShare Android store listing of this workspace: whether the listing is taken down (kind REPORT after credible reports, COPYRIGHT or TRADEMARK after a complete notice, STAFF; the public note, and whether the owner can still dispute a report takedown once in the Store tab), releases AppForShare marked unsafe (the kill switch: the public reason, the source RESCAN = the weekly malware rescan matched, REPORT = a rescan started by a malware report matched (the number of reports never marks a release unsafe), STAFF; whether it was live, in which case it is out of the store and the F-Droid compatible repository lists it as KnownVuln so clients warn people who installed it), copies at Google Play or the App Store the author must pull there by hand (AppForShare never removes them), recent reports on the listing (category, the text with links removed, date and what the automatic triage did; never who reported), and copyright or trademark notices (status DISABLED = waiting for the one response of the developer, with evidence, RESPONDED = the sender may reply once within 10 business days, DECISION = AppForShare decides Restore or Keep down, RESTORED, KEPT_DOWN = upheld, WITHDRAWN, REJECTED; sender, work, claimed infringement, the decision reason, whether it counts as upheld), whether the store account is closed (three upheld notices in 12 months) and the upheld count, and the newest asset originality check (outcome PASS, HOLD = waits for proof from the Store tab, REJECT = a famous brand or another live app icon or package id without ownership proof; reasons with the addresses found, attribution notes for free stock images). Nothing comes back on a timer. Reports, rescans and complete notices are decided automatically; a disputed notice is decided by AppForShare; staff can override. Responses and disputes are sent from the Store tab or the mailed link, never from here. Read only. Every plan with an account.

name: builder_status
title: App builder status
description: The AI app builder of this workspace: builder credits left (plan credits and pack credits, the monthly amount), the credit price of each action (design, first app, small and large edit, builds), and the builder apps (id, name, status DRAFT, DESIGNED, GENERATED). With app (an id from this list): its AI steps (DESIGN, GENERATE, EDIT with status QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED; credits used, refunded = true when a step failed and its credits came back, fix attempts, the error), its builds (platform, where it ran, status, credits, refunded), and where the next iOS and Android builds can run with plain cost words: github = Your GitHub (the customer pays their own GitHub Actions minutes, 0 credits), eas_own = Your Expo account (billed by Expo, 0 credits), eas_ours = AppForShare on Expo (credits), self_hosted = AppForShare Linux (Android only, credits); options that are not possible now say why. appleSigning = the saved Apple signing for iOS builds on eas_ours: source workspace (the workspace re-signing certificate is reused, only the profile is per app) or app (the app's own .p12), certificate and profile names and expiry, stale = true when the workspace certificate was replaced after the profile was saved (names and expiry only; it is added in the dashboard, never through this tool). workspaceCertificate = the workspace re-signing certificate and whether it can sign builds. Apps have a kind: MOBILE (Expo, iOS and Android) or WEB (Vite + React site). comments = comments on the design screens (screenId, author, fromClient = written by a client on an approval link, resolved). approvalLinks = client approval links (Pro and Team; open links per app depend on the plan): label, url, state open, revoked or expired, views, the client decision APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED with onCurrentDesign = false when the design changed since. WEB apps: webPreview.url = the current version on its own preview address (every plan; null while previews are off on the server; previews are a test host with a bar on every page, only the current and the previous version keep one), webPreview.switchedOff = true when a Free preview was switched off after webPreview.idleDays without a new version (a new version or an edit turns it back on), webPreview.usage = preview traffic this UTC month in bytes against the plan allowance (over it the preview shows an allowance page until next month), and deploy = the deploy checklist (version, hosting provider netlify or vercel, provider token saved (never shown), domain and DNS records with the live check, public env variables the code reads, secret names only), ready, and the last deploys (status, url, mock = test mode where nothing was uploaded, refunded). aiPausedUntil = set while new AI steps of the workspace wait because too many failed in 24 hours (their credits were given back); say the time. MOBILE apps: mobilePreview = the current version running in the browser (react-native-web, shown in a phone frame on the app page): url (null until ready), status PENDING or BUILDING (about a minute), READY, FAILED with error (the app itself still passed its checks), liveContent = CMSCure texts and lists load live in it; same allowance and switch off rules as web previews. Without app: packs = the credit packs (credits and price in USD cents; Pro and Team, features.creditPacks; bought by the workspace owner in the dashboard, App builder, never through this tool), canBuyPacks, nudges = plain plan notes at a limit (apps used, credits low or out) with where to go; repeat them in words, do not push. Read only. Every plan with an account; Your GitHub and Your Expo account work on every plan for iOS and Android, eas_ours is Pro and Team.

For a document (statement of work, idea doc or spec) use builder_start_from_document of the appforshare-mcp npm server, which uploads the local file and returns the same answer; pass its intake here only to change the idea of that start. appId (optional) = the app id for Google Play and the App Store (Android package and iOS bundle id, like com.yourcompany.app; it cannot change after the first store upload): ask for it only when the person has one, else the generated one is used.
